text:
Everything has been plundered, betrayed, sold.

The great black wings of death rip the air,

Misery gnaws to the bone.

How, then, not despair?


During the day, from nearby woods,

the cherries carry summer into the city.

At night, the deep transparent skies

shine with new galaxies.


And the miraculous approaches, imminent,

to the filthy ruined houses—

something that in fact no one knows,

though wild in our breast for centuries.




1921

translation.title: Everything Has Been Plundered
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the movement from devastation to the inexplicable nearness of the miraculous.
